title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Threatening Regulatory Action
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal represents a patron suing a restaurant in Small Claims Court for food poisoning. To force an early settlement, the paralegal tells the restaurant owner, "Pay my client $3,000 today, or I will report your kitchen to the Ministry of Health." Is this ethical?
options: Yes, protecting the public from health hazards is a paralegal's duty.
Yes, as long as the paralegal believes the kitchen is actually dirty.
No, a paralegal must not threaten to initiate a regulatory proceeding to gain a benefit for a client in a civil matter.
No, but the client is allowed to make this threat directly without the paralegal's involvement.
questions.explain: Rule 2.02 (Honesty and Candour) explicitly prohibits a paralegal from threatening to initiate a criminal, quasi-criminal, or regulatory charge/proceeding for the primary purpose of gaining an advantage in a civil matter.
